FIELD GUIDE / Equipment

Read your wand

First check whether a new wand can reliably draw your combination. Then check how long it can keep casting.

SPECIMEN / Visual clues

From tip to tail

Crystal tips cast in order; wooden tips shuffle. One prong means one base spell per cast, two mean two, and three mean three to six. Short, medium and long shafts hold 2–4, 5–8 and 9–12 slots. A round tail indicates high mana regeneration. Check item details for exact values.

Understanding the stats

These are the base ranges for random wands. Card time modifiers add to the base values, and your character's casting animation also affects actual firing speed.

Rune Slots 2–12 slots
How many cards you can install. Longer combinations need more slots; empty slots do not fire.
Spells per Weave 1–6
How many cards a cast initially draws. Cards such as Double Spell draw more, so the actual projectile count also depends on your arrangement.
Shuffle / No shuffle
Non-shuffle wands draw in slot order; shuffle wands randomize the deck. Start with no shuffle when learning triggers, modifiers or note combinations.
Mana Reserve 24–1200 · Mana Flow 2–320/s
Maximum mana determines whether you can afford an expensive shot; regeneration determines sustained output. Unaffordable cards may be skipped. If nothing can fire, wait for mana or change the deck.
Casting Pause 0.08–2.4 s
Base wait between casts. Cast modifiers can reduce it to zero; character attack animations and spell-specific cooldowns still limit repeated casting.
Renewal Time 0.10–6 s
After the deck finishes or wraps, the wand reloads. Recharge modifiers can stack below zero; the wait is treated as zero. Recharge and cast delay count down together, and both must finish before the next cast.
Waver 0–15°
Random deviation from the aimed direction. Each projectile has its own base spread; wand stats and modifiers such as Precision also affect the result.
Mind Conversion 20
Successful casts cost sanity equal to net mana spent / 20, with a minimum of 0.1 and never taking sanity below zero. A Starter Wand's Spark Bolt costs 5 mana and 0.25 sanity.
Always-cast modifier
Rare wands have a 10% chance, and Epic wands a 25% chance, to carry innate Speed Up or Precision. It applies each cast without using a slot.
WAND TYPES

Choosing quality and archetype

Random wands no longer use stat points. Each stat is sampled separately within its rarity range, usually near the centre; higher tiers have better typical values. Common, Fine, Rare and Epic wands have 3–7, 4–9, 6–11 and 8–12 slots respectively. Existing wands retain their stats.

SproutNo shuffle; narrower stat distributions favor balanced results.
RapidFaster casting and recharge with better regeneration, at the cost of some mana capacity and slots.
ReservoirHigher mana capacity, with slightly lower regeneration and slower recharge.
RenewalHigher regeneration, with slightly lower mana capacity and a longer cast delay.
WeaverNo shuffle and more slots, with slightly slower casting and recharge.
ChaosAlways shuffles; favors multishot, higher mana capacity and faster casting, with wider spread.

The Starter Wand has fixed stats: 2 slots, no shuffle, 1 base spell per cast, 120 mana, 18 mana/s, 0.65-second cast delay, 1.4-second recharge, and 6° spread.

Collision and timed carriers release an unused payload when they expire normally. Piercing carriers can release payloads on repeated hits. Each scatter pellet owns an independent collision or timed payload. Shorter lifetime can release it before its normal timer.

FIELD TESTS

Turn order into effects

Use a non-shuffle wand with one base spell per cast. Clear the other slots and install cards from left to right.

Example A / Two slots

Deliver an explosion

Explosion → Spark Bolt

Explosion is an impact modifier: the spark explodes when it hits, including piercing hits. It hurts friend and foe regardless of target selection and ignites objects, but does not directly damage structures, boats or docks. It is not a separate payload; wall phasing and simple expiry do not trigger it.

View Explosion modifier →
Example B / Three slots

Draw two different projectiles

Double Spell → Spark Bolt → Magic Arrow

Double Spell draws the next two cards so both projectile types fire in one cast. Double Copy instead duplicates the current group's attacks. These cards serve different purposes.
